On 10/01/2012 09:38 PM, fabio alexander sierra matamoros wrote:
> Dear Lavaan users
> I am working with ordinal data. I would like to know if is there any way
> to impute missing data?

Currently (0.5-9), lavaan only has the WLS(MV) estimator available for
ordinal data, so we can not use FIML. I would not recommend single
imputation. You could use multiple imputation, using for example the
'mice' package (probably Amelia too). Once you have those imputed
datasets, you need to run the model on each of them, and aggregate the
results using Rubin's rules. In the semTools package, there is a runMI()
function that does this automatically for continuous data. It is
probably not too hard to adapt this for ordinal data... (and that is why
I have Alex in cc).

Yves.

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: missing data - ordinal variables
parts:
Hi all,

The topic of incorporating ordinal data analysis into the runMI function has been kicked around here over the last week or two. Currently, I believe that runMI can work for ordinal data with a couple of caveats.

1. We have not explicitly tested runMI with ordinal data, so I won't promise that it will work. With that said, I'm fairly sure that runMI should be able to combine parameter estimates and standard errors in a model with ordinal data.
2. The issue with using runMI with ordinal data is computing model fit information. Currently we haven't updated runMI to incorporate the fit indices related to ordinal data. This is especially relevant for the Mplus and Meng & Rubin chi square statistics. I believe that if you request the Li, Meng, Raghunathan & Rubin chi square statistics (set chi= 'LMRR' in runMI), your models will run.

If you decide to test this out, please let me know, I'd be very curious to hear about your experience using runMI with ordinal data and any suggestions you have.

Thanks,

-Alex

semTools: https://github.com/simsem/semTools/wiki

On 10/05/2012 04:41 PM, djoubert wrote:
> Do you know missForest? It's a great and simple to use package; I have
> used it many times in the past and the algorithm seems very effective.
> Use missForest to get an "updated" (imputed) dataset and then use Lavaan
> to run your analyses.

That would be *single* imputation. And although that is ok for getting
parameter estimates only, you can not trust the standard errors (or the
test statistic). For that, you need *multiple* imputations. So you do
this multiple times (say, 10 times), and then you need to aggregate the
results. How to do the latter is what the runMI() function does in the
semTools package.

Yves.
